answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because mirror only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any cipher approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
